header.name: Meta-learning
header.description: Meta-learning will cover recent research papers focusing on the broad goal of out-of-distribution generalization in machine-learning. Thus, in addition to the basic model, metric and optimization based meta-learning techniques, we will also cover papers at the intersection of meta-learning and continual learning, representation learning,  test-time adaptation and neurosymbolic reasoning. We will apply these techniques to solve reppresentative problems in few-shot, online and analogical learning/reasoning.
prerequisites_mandatory: At least one of the following courses: ECE363/ECE563/CSE343/CSE543/CSE342/CSE542/ECE356/ECE556/CSE642/ECE553/CSE641
prerequisites_desirable: Experience in developing neural network models using pytorch
prerequisites_mandatory_resolved: At least one of the following courses: ECE363/ECE563/CSE343/CSE543/CSE342/CSE542/ECE356/ECE556/CSE642/ECE553/CSE641
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: Experience in developing neural network models using pytorch

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Understanding of basic meta-learning techniques and proficieny at applying meta-learning to any new machine-learning problem. Ability to apply these techniques to real-life problems.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Understanding the challenges of out-of-distribution generalization and continual learning in supervised learning, and familiarity with a approaches such as generative replay, neuromodulation, test-time adaptation, etc. and meta-learning techniques used to address these challenges. Ability to use these techniques to attack real-life problems.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Understanding the challenges of analogical reasoning, and approaches such as neuo-symbolic techniques and program synthesis as well as the use of LLMs to augment these.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Experience of attempting to generalize/combine ideas from multiple papers as well as with other ideas of one’s own and validate/invalidate these on the challenge problems posed in the course assignments, i.e.,taking the first steps towards research.
